description: TLCTC #1 Abuse of Functions — a designed feature is used outside its intended boundaries. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#abuse-of-functions
TLCTC #2 Exploiting Server — a server-role component has a coding/implementation flaw. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#exploiting-server
TLCTC #3 Exploiting Client — a client-role component has a coding/implementation flaw. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#exploiting-client
TLCTC #4 Identity Theft — a credential, key, or session artifact is stolen, forged, or applied. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#identity-theft
TLCTC #5 Man in the Middle — a communication path is intercepted, relayed, or altered. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#man-in-the-middle
TLCTC #6 Flooding Attack — resources are exhausted by volume. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#flooding-attack
TLCTC #7 Malware — foreign executable content runs in the target system. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#malware
TLCTC #8 Physical Attack — a physical/local attack vector compromises the system. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#physical-attack
TLCTC #9 Social Engineering — a human is manipulated into taking an attacker-desired action. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#social-engineering
TLCTC #10 Supply Chain Attack — a trusted artifact carrying attacker control is accepted. See https://www.tlctc.net/tlctc-10-definitions.html#supply-chain-attack
